source.title: Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization
source.author: Francesco Orabona

independence.restriction: Graph constructed freshly from pinned raw PDF13–14 text and actual pixels. Cover PDF1 used only for metadata. Governance protocols consulted; no implementation declarations/proofs or historical acceptance verdicts used to construct topology.

render_warnings: Cover render reported missing display-font aliases Symbol/ArialUnicode; actual cover pixels readable. No formula render failure observed in pp1–2.
scope: iid unit-interval guessing, expected-fixed comparator minimum, population mean/variance benchmark, causal expected excess and normalized criterion, with every other substantive item on printed1–2 explicitly classified.

contracts.statement: For rounds t=1,...,T the adversary chooses y_t in[0,1] secretly; the player chooses x_t in[0,1]; then y_t is revealed and loss(x_t-y_t)^2 is paid. In the stochastic simplification Y_t are iid from one fixed distribution on[0,1], chosen at game start.
contracts.quantifiers: Any fixed distribution on[0,1]; positive finite integer T implicit in the averaged display. Player predicts before observing current target. The source does not formalize policy class, sigma algebra or external seed.
contracts.limits: Unknown distribution is fixed, not reselected adaptively each round. The initial general game allows arbitrary targets, but the iid assertions do not extend to arbitrary/adversarial targets.

contracts.statement: If the distribution were known, predicting its population mean each round incurs expected cumulative loss sigma²T, and the player cannot do better.
contracts.notation: Let m=E[Y_1] and sigma²=Var(Y_1) denote analyst notation for the source's mean and variance; m is not introduced as a printed symbol on these pages.
contracts.quantifiers: One fixed deterministic population mean at every round; causal strategy lower-bound interpretation is relative to game information. No pointwise, high-probability or realized-path optimality is stated.
contracts.limits: This is a known-distribution oracle benchmark, not an algorithm supplied to the unknown-distribution learner; no empirical-mean algorithm is specified on pp1–2.

contracts.order: min_x E[sum loss(x,Y_t)], with one deterministic x held fixed across all rounds and all outcomes. Expectation averages the iid targets; x_t may depend on previous revealed targets under the game.
contracts.limits: Not E[min_x sum loss], not sum_t min_x E[loss] as a printed formula, and not minimization over history-dependent strategies. Mean attainment is asserted via surrounding prose; an sInf/IsLeast representation or uniqueness theorem is not printed.

contracts.expectation_scope: Printed expectation subscripts name Y_1,...,Y_T. An independent randomized learner seed and integration over it are not explicitly provided.
contracts.limits: Causal/nonanticipating prediction is essential to the stated game interpretation. Mere iid targets and arbitrary correlated prediction variables do not justify nonnegativity. Pathwise best-fixed regret need not be nonnegative.

contracts.statement: Call a strategy successful if(1.1) grows sublinearly with time, equivalently if(1.2) tends to0 as T tends to infinity. On average across rounds the algorithm approaches optimal performance.
contracts.analyst_reading: Writing Delta_T for(1.1), normalized excess is Delta_T/T for T>0; success means Delta_T/T→0.
contracts.limits: No specific learner is proved to satisfy this condition and no rate is provided here. No almost-sure convergence, per-round convergence, finite-horizon uniform guarantee or stopping-time assertion is printed. T=0 normalization is unspecified.

contracts.statement: Remove assumptions on data generation and consider arbitrary y_t sequences. If the algorithm is deterministic, remove expectation; winning is sublinear regret against the best single choice in hindsight.
contracts.limits: This is a definitional/model transition, not a theorem exchanging expectation and minimum. For randomized algorithms the page does not specify the expectation convention. Fixed-comparator expected loss and pathwise minimum are different benchmarks.

contracts.formula: Regret_T(u):=sum_{t=1}^T ell_t(x_t)-sum_{t=1}^T ell_t(u); for every fixed u in V, lim_{T→∞} Regret_T(u)/T <=0.
contracts.statement: V subset R^d, losses ell_t:V→R; comparator u fixed. The algorithm does not know u or corresponding regret to guarantee a bound. Remark1.1 suppresses loss-sequence dependence. Footnote1 permits predictions in a larger W in some cases.
contracts.limits: This ordinary-limit inequality for signed generic comparator regret is distinct from the stochastic nonnegative excess tending to0. The source does not provide a limsup, absolute-regret, nonnegative-regret or eventual-epsilon equivalence here; no such conversion is added.

source_gaps.claim: Well-defined probability, measurability and finite expectation infrastructure is omitted.
source_gaps.missing: A common probability space/law, measurable observations/predictions, and justification that bounded[0,1] squared losses and their finite sums are integrable. The informal interval game supplies boundedness but not a formal construction.
source_gaps.not_an_extra_public_premise: Integrability should be supplied from the source model, not imported as a desired loss identity or lower-bound premise.

source_gaps.claim: Population mean is feasible and attains the minimum expected fixed-comparator loss sigma²T.
source_gaps.missing: The source gives no proof of m in[0,1], expected square at m equals variance, or E sum(x-Y_t)^2>=sigma²T with equality at m. The deterministic bias/variance calculation and finite-sum expectation accounting are omitted.
source_gaps.not_printed: No displayed squared-loss decomposition, minimizer uniqueness proof, sInf/IsLeast identity, or library implementation route is present.

source_gaps.claim: No admissible causal player beats the mean benchmark in expectation; excess is nonnegative.
source_gaps.missing: A formal admissible information/policy class and proof connecting prediction-before-reveal plus iid sampling to the lower bound. Strict-past measurability, independence/conditional-expectation cancellation and extension to a private random seed are not developed.
source_gaps.not_printed: The identity Delta_T=sum E[(x_t-m)^2] is a possible derived explanation, not a displayed/source-proved statement on these pages. No seed measurability or seed-target independence assumptions are printed.

source_gaps.claim: Average excess equals cumulative excess divided byT, so sublinearity and normalized convergence are equivalent.
source_gaps.missing: Routine positive-T algebra and a precise sequence-level meaning of sublinearity are not proved. The source uses the equivalence informally and supplies no T=0 convention.

source_gaps.claim: The hindsight minimum in the deterministic definition is attained by a best fixed action.
source_gaps.missing: No minimizer/existence proof is given on pp1–2. This contextual source gap is separate from the population-mean expected minimum and not discharged using unread adjacent pages.

assumption_delta_ledger.detail: IID fixed distribution on[0,1] chosen at game start.
Game order implies player lacks current target. Formal filtration/strict-past policy type absent.
Finite expectations need formal measurable RVs; bounded source losses should discharge integrability. No implementation bundle evaluated.
No private-seed law, independence or averaging convention specified. Do not silently claim all randomized/adaptive policies.
Sampling distribution over[0,1] supplies the range/support. Source does not distinguish pointwise from almost-sure real-RV representations or impose all-null-history behavior.
Required to justify printed oracle and min-E benchmark, asserted without proof.
Averaged display uses1/T; no zero-horizon convention or off-source extension supplied.
Only population mean benchmark here; empirical-prefix learner and sample-mean minimizer not provided in this extract.
Stochastic success is normalized excess→0. Generic comparator no-regret separately prints ordinary lim<=0; do not substitute limsup or claim the criteria interchangeable.

not_source_claims: No displayed causal excess decomposition sum E[(x_t-m)^2].
No empirical-mean algorithm or convergence rate proof.
No uniqueness theorem, complete strategy-class construction or randomized minimax theorem.
No min/E interchange and no nonnegativity claim for pathwise regret.
No Lean signature, library route or proof-term topology is extracted.
